sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》节目。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantham.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: When you're the parent of a small child, it's not uncommon to have an experience like this.
sentences.zh: 当你是一个小孩的家长时，经历这样的事情并不罕见。

sentences.en: Your kid comes home from preschool and says,
sentences.zh: 你的孩子从幼儿园回家说：

sentences.en: the butterfly flew away.
sentences.zh: 蝴蝶飞走了。

sentences.en: You go, what butterfly?
sentences.zh: 你问，什么蝴蝶？

sentences.en: And your child looks at you puzzled.
sentences.zh: 然后你的孩子困惑地看着你。

sentences.en: She doesn't realize that the butterfly she saw at preschool,
sentences.zh: 她没有意识到，她在幼儿园看到的蝴蝶，

sentences.en: when you were not around, is not a butterfly you know anything about.
sentences.zh: 在你不在场的时候，并不是你所知道的任何蝴蝶。

sentences.en: In the minds of very small children,
sentences.zh: 在幼儿的心智中，

sentences.en: there is no sharp line between what they know and what others know.
sentences.zh: 他们所知的和他人所知的之间并没有明确的界限。

sentences.en: But at some point early in childhood, all of us made a magical discovery.
sentences.zh: 但在童年早期的某个时刻，我们所有人都做出了一个神奇的发现。

sentences.en: Our thoughts belong only to us.
sentences.zh: 我们的思想只属于我们自己。

sentences.en: Parents, siblings, teachers, no one can enter our minds and see what we are thinking.
sentences.zh: 父母、兄弟姐妹、老师，没有人能进入我们的内心，看到我们在想什么。

sentences.en: A second discovery follows shortly afterward.
sentences.zh: 不久之后，第二个发现随之而来。

sentences.en: If no one can see what is happening inside our minds,
sentences.zh: 如果没人能看到我们内心在发生什么，

sentences.en: we can hide things from other people.
sentences.zh: 我们就可以对别人隐瞒事情。

sentences.en: We can keep secrets.
sentences.zh: 我们可以保守秘密。

sentences.en: So the pain of keeping this secret has been one of the biggest challenges I've had to deal with in my adult life.
sentences.zh: 所以，保守这个秘密的痛苦，是我成年生活中不得不面对的最大挑战之一。

sentences.en: I do think constantly about it, and I can't tell anybody about it now.
sentences.zh: 我确实一直在想这件事，而且我现在不能告诉任何人。

sentences.en: Because I'm afraid of what might happen,
sentences.zh: 因为我害怕会发生什么，

sentences.en: and it's affected my overall well-being.
sentences.zh: 这影响了我的整体幸福感。

sentences.en: This week on Hidden Brain,
sentences.zh: 本周的《隐藏的大脑》，

sentences.en: how secrets tether us to our past,
sentences.zh: 秘密如何将我们与过去捆绑在一起，

sentences.en: and sometimes keep us from stepping into the future.
sentences.zh: 有时又如何阻碍我们迈向未来。

sentences.en: So often, the secrets that we keep start out as something small.
sentences.zh: 很多时候，我们保守的秘密最初都是些小事。

sentences.en: We make tiny edits to our personal narratives.
sentences.zh: 我们对个人经历做些微小的修饰。

sentences.en: We skip over little details about where we come from,
sentences.zh: 我们略过关于我们来自哪里、

sentences.en: what we've done, and who we know.
sentences.zh: 做过什么、认识谁的一些小细节。

sentences.en: We hide pieces of ourselves that produce shame or anxiety.
sentences.zh: 我们隐藏起自己身上那些会产生羞耻感或焦虑的部分。

sentences.en: But over time, the weight of even small secrets can become burdensome.
sentences.zh: 但随着时间的推移，即使是小秘密的重量也会变得沉重不堪。

sentences.en: Lauren LeDuc knows exactly how this works.
sentences.zh: 劳伦·勒杜克非常清楚这是怎么回事。

sentences.en: She's in her early 20s and works in a pharmacy.
sentences.zh: 她二十出头，在一家药店工作。

sentences.en: But I'm also a fiancé, a daughter, a sibling, an older sibling to seven.
sentences.zh: 但我也是一个未婚妻、一个女儿、一个姐妹，是七个孩子中的长姐。

sentences.en: I'm also a student.
sentences.zh: 我还是个学生。

sentences.en: I'm in my master's, trying to get into medical school at the moment.
sentences.zh: 我正在读硕士，目前正努力考入医学院。

sentences.en: Lauren's secret has to do with religion.
sentences.zh: 劳伦的秘密与宗教有关。

sentences.en: She was raised Catholic.
sentences.zh: 她是在天主教环境下长大的。

sentences.en: When she was a teenager, she turned away from Catholicism.
sentences.zh: 十几岁时，她背离了天主教。

sentences.en: But she didn't want to give up on religion altogether.
sentences.zh: 但她并不想完全放弃宗教信仰。

sentences.en: I just didn't know what to believe in,
sentences.zh: 我只是不知道该相信什么，

sentences.en: but I knew that I was still believing in God.
sentences.zh: 但我知道我仍然相信上帝。

sentences.en: She started to explore other faiths, Islam, Judaism, Buddhism.
sentences.zh: 她开始探索其他信仰，伊斯兰教、犹太教、佛教。

sentences.en: She sought out people from different religious traditions
sentences.zh: 她寻找来自不同宗教传统的人，

sentences.en: and peppered them with questions.
sentences.zh: 并向他们抛出一连串的问题。

sentences.en: For example, I would try and find someone in high school
sentences.zh: 例如，我会试着在高中

sentences.en: or on my campus that was a practicing Buddhist
sentences.zh: 或校园里找一个虔诚的佛教徒，

sentences.en: and just ask questions about that religion.
sentences.zh: 然后问一些关于那个宗教的问题。

sentences.en: One of her religious consultants was a boy named Hamza.
sentences.zh: 她的一位宗教顾问是一个叫哈姆扎的男孩。

sentences.en: I was on student council.
sentences.zh: 我当时在学生会。

sentences.en: He was on, like, the media production team.
sentences.zh: 他当时在媒体制作团队之类的部门。

sentences.en: And we were actually playing a kickball game.
sentences.zh: 我们当时正在玩踢球游戏。

sentences.en: And he scored a home run.
sentences.zh: 他打出了一个全垒打。

sentences.en: And sophomore me was like, oh, that's the coolest guy ever.
sentences.zh: 大二时的我心想，哇，那真是最酷的家伙。

sentences.en: Hamza, in addition to being the coolest guy ever, was Muslim.
sentences.zh: 哈姆扎不仅是最酷的家伙，还是个穆斯林。

sentences.en: It was nice to have someone who was actually faithfully a part of their religion,
sentences.zh: 能有一个真正虔诚地信仰自己宗教的人真好，

sentences.en: whose family practiced it, who he seemed to really enjoy it.
sentences.zh: 他的家人也信奉这个，而且他看起来真的很享受。

sentences.en: Hamza and Lauren began dating some months later.
sentences.zh: 几个月后，哈姆扎和劳伦开始约会。

sentences.en: Eventually, as she spoke with him and other practicing Muslims
sentences.zh: 最终，当她与他以及其他虔诚的穆斯林交谈，

sentences.en: about what it meant to be a person of faith,
sentences.zh: 讨论作为一名信徒意味着什么时，

sentences.en: Lauren decided that Islam was the right fit for her.
sentences.zh: 劳伦认为伊斯兰教非常适合她。

sentences.en: In her senior year of high school, she converted.
sentences.zh: 高中最后一年，她皈依了。

sentences.en: This was when her dilemma began.
sentences.zh: 这时她的困境开始了。

sentences.en: She didn't want people to assume that Hamza was the reason she had embraced Islam.
sentences.zh: 她不想让人们认为哈姆扎是她皈依伊斯兰教的原因。

sentences.en: Where they think, I did it for a boy.
sentences.zh: 他们会觉得，我是为了一个男孩才这么做的。

sentences.en: So, she decided to fudge one tiny detail.
sentences.zh: 所以，她决定编造一个微小的细节。

sentences.en: Whenever I meet people and they ask about this, I ultimately end up emphasizing the point,
sentences.zh: 每当我遇到人，他们问起这件事时，我最终都会强调一点：

sentences.en: yes, I converted before I met him.
sentences.zh: 是的，我在认识他之前就皈依了。

sentences.en: But that's not how it happened.
sentences.zh: 但事实并非如此。

sentences.en: It was the other way around.
sentences.zh: 情况恰恰相反。

sentences.en: I met my boyfriend and then I converted.
sentences.zh: 我先认识了男朋友，然后才皈依的。

sentences.en: I see.
sentences.zh: 我明白了。

sentences.en: The conversion is not the secret, but the timing of the conversion,
sentences.zh: 皈依本身不是秘密，但皈依的时间点是，

sentences.en: you're actually, in some ways, you're predating when you actually converted
sentences.zh: 你在某种程度上把皈依的时间提前了，

sentences.en: because of your concerns about how people will perceive you.
sentences.zh: 因为你担心人们会如何看待你。

sentences.en: Yes, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: If people thought Lauren had converted to please her boyfriend,
sentences.zh: 如果人们认为劳伦皈依是为了取悦她的男朋友，

sentences.en: she worried they might make other assumptions about her.
sentences.zh: 她担心他们可能会对她做出其他假设。

sentences.en: She just does whatever she's told.
sentences.zh: 她只是听从别人的吩咐。

sentences.en: She's gullible.
sentences.zh: 她很容易受骗。

sentences.en: She doesn't have her own set of values or her own thinking.
sentences.zh: 她没有自己的价值观或独立思考能力。

sentences.en: And she just did this for a boy.
sentences.zh: 她只是为了一个男孩才这么做的。

sentences.en: She's hopeless, romantic.
sentences.zh: 她是个无可救药的浪漫主义者。

sentences.en: So, for anyone to identify me with those traits, it would just be so hurtful.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果有人把这些特质与我联系在一起，那会非常伤人。

sentences.en: To my self-esteem, to my confidence.
sentences.zh: 伤害我的自尊心，伤害我的自信心。

sentences.en: Lauren saw herself as motivated, strong.
sentences.zh: 劳伦认为自己积极进取、坚强。

sentences.en: Decisive.
sentences.zh: 果断。

sentences.en: And when it came to religion, she knew her choices were entirely her own.
sentences.zh: 当涉及到宗教时，她知道自己的选择完全是她自己的。

sentences.en: How I view religion, it's just me and God.
sentences.zh: 我如何看待宗教，那只是我和上帝之间的事。

sentences.en: It shouldn't involve anyone else.
sentences.zh: 它不应该涉及其他人。

sentences.en: It should just be a one-on-one relationship.
sentences.zh: 它应该只是一种一对一的关系。

sentences.en: At first, the little lie made everything easier.
sentences.zh: 起初，这个小谎言让一切变得简单。

sentences.en: She didn't have to explain to people that she would have made the same choice
sentences.zh: 她不必向人们解释，无论是否和哈姆扎在一起，

sentences.en: whether or not she was with Hamza.
sentences.zh: 她都会做出同样的选择。

sentences.en: Just don't tell them.
sentences.zh: 别告诉他们。

sentences.en: Tell them a short synopsis.
sentences.zh: 告诉他们一个简短的梗概。

sentences.en: Make it easy and to the point.
sentences.zh: 简单明了就好。

sentences.en: Easy and to the point.
sentences.zh: 简单明了。

sentences.en: That was the hope.
sentences.zh: 这就是当时的希望。

sentences.en: But like many secrets, this one slowly took on a life of its own.
sentences.zh: 但像许多秘密一样，这个秘密慢慢有了自己的生命。

sentences.en: After high school, Lauren got a job as a pharmacy technician.
sentences.zh: 高中毕业后，劳伦找到了一份药房技术员的工作。

sentences.en: When I talked to her, she had been working at the pharmacy for more than four years.
sentences.zh: 我和她交谈时，她已经在药房工作了四年多。

sentences.en: The altered timeline for her religious conversion was the story she shared with colleagues.
sentences.zh: 关于她宗教皈依的虚假时间线，就是她与同事分享的故事。

sentences.en: But as time passed, the little lie became harder to manage.
sentences.zh: 但随着时间的推移，这个小谎言变得越来越难应付。

sentences.en: Somebody was talking about me and Hamza and the timeline of like how we met.
sentences.zh: 有人在谈论我和哈姆扎，以及我们相识的时间线。

sentences.en: And I was like, oh crap, what did I tell them?
sentences.zh: 我当时心想，糟了，我告诉过他们什么？

sentences.en: I need to make sure that my story is correct.
sentences.zh: 我得确保我的说法是正确的。

sentences.en: Because I told them maybe a year ago one story.
sentences.zh: 因为我可能一年前告诉过他们一个版本。

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.en: So I'm like having to keep track of like what I'm saying.
sentences.zh: 所以我得时刻留意我说了什么。

sentences.en: And that's something that I do fear.
sentences.zh: 这也是我所担心的。

sentences.en: That I told somebody something maybe a year ago about our relationship.
sentences.zh: 我担心我一年前可能告诉过某人关于我们关系的事情。

sentences.en: And then they catch me on it.
sentences.zh: 然后他们抓住了我的把柄。

sentences.en: Soon, there was another complication.
sentences.zh: 很快，又出现了另一个复杂情况。

sentences.en: Hamza.
sentences.zh: 哈姆扎。

sentences.en: He just flat out tells people that this is whenever we started dating.
sentences.zh: 他直接告诉别人我们是什么时候开始约会的。

sentences.en: And then I converted and then we got engaged.
sentences.zh: 然后我皈依了，接着我们订婚了。

sentences.en: So he doesn't mind.
sentences.zh: 所以他不在乎。

sentences.en: He's not afraid of people.
sentences.zh: 他不怕别人怎么看。

sentences.en: So he just tells them the exact story.
sentences.zh: 所以他只是告诉他们真实的故事。

sentences.en: Which is also kind of scary for me because I'm like, oh my gosh.
sentences.zh: 这对我来说也有点可怕，因为我心想，天哪。

sentences.en: What if one of your people comes to me?
sentences.zh: 如果你的熟人来问我怎么办？

sentences.en: And then, you know, I'm like, Hamza, stop.
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道，我会说，哈姆扎，停下。

sentences.en: We have to go with my story.
sentences.zh: 我们必须坚持我的版本。

sentences.en: And he's like, people probably already know.
sentences.zh: 他说，人们可能早就知道了。

sentences.en: And like they don't know because I'm telling them this.
sentences.zh: 但他们并不知道，因为我告诉他们的是这个版本，

sentences.en: And you're telling them that.
sentences.zh: 而你告诉他们的是那个版本。

sentences.en: Lauren's worries started to spill into her life.
sentences.zh: 劳伦的担忧开始蔓延到她的生活中。

sentences.en: There were nights she couldn't sleep as she tried to remember all the angles.
sentences.zh: 有几个晚上她彻夜难眠，试图记住所有的细节。

sentences.en: What she'd said to whom, what Hamza may have said, how people might cross-reference the stories and discover the truth.
sentences.zh: 她对谁说了什么，哈姆扎可能说了什么，人们可能会如何交叉核对这些故事并发现真相。

sentences.en: And then her worst fears were realized.
sentences.zh: 然后她最担心的事发生了。

sentences.en: We know this one couple, a husband and wife.
sentences.zh: 我们认识一对夫妇，丈夫和妻子。

sentences.en: And I guess he told the husband and the husband told the wife.
sentences.zh: 我想他告诉了丈夫，丈夫又告诉了妻子。

sentences.en: And then the wife was asking me one day, oh yeah, how did y'all get together and tell me your story?
sentences.zh: 有一天妻子问我，哦对了，你们俩是怎么在一起的，告诉我你的故事？

sentences.en: And she's one of the less conservative people that I know.
sentences.zh: 她是我认识的人中比较开明的一个。

sentences.en: And she's also a Muslim.
sentences.zh: 她也是个穆斯林。

sentences.en: But I was telling her the shortened version.
sentences.zh: 但我当时告诉她的是简化版。

sentences.en: And she's like, you know, my husband told me something different.
sentences.zh: 她说，你知道吗，我丈夫告诉我的不一样。

sentences.en: The other woman was understanding.
sentences.zh: 那位女士很理解。

sentences.en: She assumed Lauren had made up the story in order not to offend conservative relatives who didn't know when Lauren and Hamza started dating.
sentences.zh: 她以为劳伦编造这个故事是为了不冒犯那些不知道劳伦和哈姆扎何时开始约会的保守亲戚。

sentences.en: But increasingly, Lauren found the mental gymnastics of keeping her secret exhausting.
sentences.zh: 但劳伦越来越觉得保守这个秘密的心理博弈令人精疲力竭。

sentences.en: She also started to feel bad about misleading people.
sentences.zh: 她也开始为误导别人感到难过。

sentences.en: She felt really bad about deceiving one particular co-worker who had become a friend.
sentences.zh: 她为欺骗了一位已经成为朋友的同事感到非常内疚。

sentences.en: She's amazing.
sentences.zh: 她太棒了。

sentences.en: Every time I come to the pharmacy now, she's like, hey, bestie.
sentences.zh: 现在每次我来药房，她都会说，嘿，闺蜜。

sentences.en: And we really bonded because we both have dogs and our love for dogs, which is really awesome.
sentences.zh: 我们真的建立了深厚的友谊，因为我们都有狗，而且都热爱狗狗，这真的很棒。

sentences.en: But it's interesting that I'm wondering how this person at the pharmacy would feel if she knew that you had lied to her about something trivial.
sentences.zh: 但有趣的是，我在想，如果药房里的这个人知道你为了琐事对她撒了谎，她会怎么想？

sentences.en: How do you think that she would take that?
sentences.zh: 你觉得她会怎么看？

sentences.en: So part of my anxiety right now that I'm actively having is what will people think whenever they hear this?
sentences.zh: 所以我现在正经历的焦虑部分源于：当人们听到这些时会怎么想？

sentences.en: Will they think that I've been lying to them or I haven't been a faithful friend or co-worker?
sentences.zh: 他们会认为我一直在对他们撒谎，或者我不是一个忠诚的朋友或同事吗？

sentences.en: How will they react?
sentences.zh: 他们会作何反应？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, in your case, I think the lie is sort of a relatively trivial thing.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，就你的情况而言，我觉得这个谎言相对来说是一件微不足道的小事。

sentences.en: But I can see how in life there are people who put on roles and put on acts and basically, you know, live those roles and acts not for, you know, months and weeks, but for years,
sentences.zh: 但我能理解，生活中确实有人会戴着面具、演着戏，基本上，你知道，他们活在那些面具和戏码里，不是几个月或几周，而是几年，

sentences.en: for decades.
sentences.zh: 甚至是几十年。

sentences.en: And then, you know, 30 years, 40 years, 50 years on, they've essentially feel like they've lived an inauthentic life.
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道，30年、40年、50年过去了，他们本质上会觉得自己过着一种虚假的人生。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So that is something that I want to avoid.
sentences.zh: 所以这是我想要避免的事情。

sentences.en: One of those key words there, inauthentic life.
sentences.zh: 其中的一个关键词就是：虚假的人生。

sentences.en: So I'm still young and where I consider myself young.
sentences.zh: 我还很年轻，至少我认为自己还年轻。
我今年22岁。

sentences.en: So I definitely want to just get this behind me and be okay and open with accepting who I actually am and my actual timeline in life and stop fabricating this timeline because that's one step closer to just becoming me,
sentences.zh: 所以我绝对想把这件事抛在脑后，坦然面对并公开接受真实的自我，以及我生命中真实的时间线，停止编造这个时间线，因为那离成为真正的我更近了一步，

sentences.en: Lauren,
sentences.zh: 劳伦，

sentences.en: and not keeping this lie and being afraid of the timeline that I've had in life.
sentences.zh: 而不是守着这个谎言，对我在生活中经历的时间线感到恐惧。

sentences.en: I think it'll even bring me even closer to my religion if I'm just super accepting of why I converted, when I converted, and how I did it.
sentences.zh: 我想，如果我能完全接受自己皈依的原因、时间以及方式，这甚至会让我与我的宗教信仰更加亲近。

sentences.en: Lauren's secret started out small, but it gradually took up more and more mental space.
sentences.zh: 劳伦的秘密起初很小，但它逐渐占据了她越来越多的心理空间。

sentences.en: It left her feeling isolated from people who mattered to her.
sentences.zh: 这让她感到与那些对她重要的人产生了隔阂。

sentences.en: And that, it turns out, is the rub when it comes to secrets.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，这正是秘密带来的症结所在。

sentences.en: When we come back, we speak with a researcher who studies secrets and ask him to analyze Lauren's story.
sentences.zh: 稍后回来，我们将采访一位研究秘密的学者，请他分析劳伦的故事。

sentences.en: He also explains what psychological studies reveal about the consequences of secret keeping.
sentences.zh: 他还将解释心理学研究揭示的保守秘密的后果。

sentences.en: It's not having to hide a secret.
sentences.zh: 问题的关键不在于必须隐藏秘密。

sentences.en: It's having to live with it alone.
sentences.zh: 而在于必须独自承受它。

sentences.en: You're listening to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 你正在收听的是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedanta.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: Stay with us.
sentences.zh: 请继续收听。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedanta.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: Michael Slepian is a psychologist at Columbia Business School.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔·斯莱皮安是哥伦比亚商学院的一位心理学家。

sentences.en: He studies secrets.
sentences.zh: 他专门研究秘密。

sentences.en: Across a number of research studies, he finds that holding onto secrets has profound effects on our well-being,
sentences.zh: 通过多项研究，他发现保守秘密对我们的幸福感有着深远的影响，

sentences.en: but not for the reason most of us think.
sentences.zh: 但原因并非我们大多数人所想的那样。

sentences.en: Michael Slepian, welcome to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔·斯莱皮安，欢迎来到《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: It's good to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴来到这里。

sentences.en: When most of us think of keeping secrets, Michael, or the challenge of keeping secrets,
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，当我们大多数人想到保守秘密，或者保守秘密的挑战时，

sentences.en: what do we think about?
sentences.zh: 我们通常会想到什么？

sentences.en: When we think about a secret, sort of what people tend to imagine is one person sitting in a room with another person,
sentences.zh: 当我们想到秘密时，人们往往会想象一个人坐在房间里和另一个人交谈，

sentences.en: and you're talking about something related to the secret,
sentences.zh: 你们正在谈论与那个秘密相关的事情，

sentences.en: and the person with the secret has to carefully dodge questions and, you know,
sentences.zh: 而那个有秘密的人必须小心翼翼地回避问题，你知道，

sentences.en: make sure to not reveal the wrong information.
sentences.zh: 确保不泄露错误的信息。

sentences.en: And, you know, that certainly happens sometimes, but it turns out we don't actually have to hide our secrets very frequently.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这种情况确实时有发生，但事实证明，我们实际上并不需要频繁地隐藏我们的秘密。

sentences.en: It also turns out to be not the reason why they hurt us.
sentences.zh: 事实也证明，这并不是它们伤害我们的原因。

sentences.en: I'm thinking, actually, of the scene from the TV show The Marvelous Mrs. Maisel,
sentences.zh: 我其实想到了电视剧《了不起的麦瑟尔夫人》中的一个场景，

sentences.en: which I think encapsulates the conventional way most of us think of secrets.
sentences.zh: 我认为它概括了我们大多数人对秘密的传统看法。

sentences.en: One of the characters, whose name is Rose, is trying to find out information about her son, Noah.
sentences.zh: 其中一个角色，名叫罗斯，正试图打听她儿子诺亚的消息。

sentences.en: He has a top-secret job at a top-secret agency,
sentences.zh: 他在一个绝密机构从事着绝密工作，

sentences.en: and Rose is trying to get her daughter-in-law, Astrid, to spill the beans.
sentences.zh: 而罗斯正试图让她的儿媳阿斯特丽德说出实情。

sentences.en: So, you call his university the company?
sentences.zh: 所以，你管他的大学叫“公司”？

sentences.en: Sorry, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 抱歉，我不知道。

sentences.en: Or the other place he works is the company?
sentences.zh: 还是说他工作的另一个地方叫“公司”？

sentences.en: Wait, did I say there was another place?
sentences.zh: 等等，我有说过还有另一个地方吗？

sentences.en: He lied, didn't he?
sentences.zh: 他撒谎了，对吧？

sentences.en: No, I didn't mean to.
sentences.zh: 不，我不是故意的。

sentences.en: Oh, well, does he keep in touch when he's away?
sentences.zh: 哦，好吧，他离开的时候会保持联系吗？

sentences.en: He usually can't.
sentences.zh: 他通常没法联系。

sentences.en: But if he's away and you need to reach him, are you able to?
sentences.zh: 但如果他不在，你需要联系他，你能联系上吗？

sentences.en: Not really.
sentences.zh: 不太行。

sentences.en: What would you do in an emergency?
sentences.zh: 如果发生紧急情况你会怎么办？

sentences.en: Well, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我不知道。

sentences.en: I can't just dial the operator and say, give me the CIA.
sentences.zh: 我不能直接拨通接线员说，帮我接中情局。

sentences.en: It doesn't work that way.
sentences.zh: 事情不是那样运作的。

sentences.en: Of course not.
sentences.zh: 当然不是。

sentences.en: And Michael, of course, this is what we think when we think about keeping secrets,
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，当然，这就是我们想到保守秘密时所想到的，

sentences.en: the moment of trying to hide something from someone and feeling flustered as they fish it out of us.
sentences.zh: 那一刻我们试图对某人隐瞒某事，并因对方的盘问而感到慌乱。

sentences.en: Yeah, and so if that was all that was harmful about secrecy,
sentences.zh: 是的，如果保守秘密的危害仅限于此，

sentences.en: that would actually be quite good because we're not often in these conversations.
sentences.zh: 那其实还挺好的，因为我们并不常处于这种对话中。

sentences.en: But unfortunately, even when we're not talking to someone about something related to the secret,
sentences.zh: 但不幸的是，即使我们没有和别人谈论与秘密相关的事情，

sentences.en: we have all the time in the world to simply think about that secret
sentences.zh: 我们也有大把的时间去单纯地思考那个秘密，

sentences.en: and for our mind to return to that secret again and again.
sentences.zh: 让我们的思绪一次又一次地回到那个秘密上。

sentences.en: And this is where the real harm of secrecy seems to seep in.
sentences.zh: 而这似乎才是秘密真正造成伤害的地方。

sentences.en: Not moments when you have to hide the secret,
sentences.zh: 不是在你必须隐藏秘密的时刻，

sentences.en: but moments when you find yourself just having to think about it.
sentences.zh: 而是当你发现自己不得不去想它的时刻。

sentences.en: And you find this in a number of studies that no one is usually behaving like the nosy mom.
sentences.zh: 你在多项研究中发现，通常没人会表现得像个爱管闲事的妈妈。

sentences.en: No one's asking us to reveal our secret because, of course,
sentences.zh: 没人要求我们泄露秘密，因为当然，

sentences.en: they don't even know that we have a secret.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至不知道我们有秘密。

sentences.en: Yeah, you know, you could think about sort of a common secret, for example, is, say, infidelity.
sentences.zh: 是的，你知道，你可以想想一个常见的秘密，比如，不忠。

sentences.en: That's not a thing we go around asking our friends and family about.
sentences.zh: 这不是我们会到处去问朋友和家人的事情。

sentences.en: Hey, have you ever cheated on your partner?
sentences.zh: 嘿，你有没有背叛过你的伴侣？

sentences.en: It just doesn't work that way.
sentences.zh: 事情根本不是那样运作的。

sentences.en: So if concealing the truth from prying eyes is not what makes secret keeping hard or keeping secrets hard,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果向窥探的目光隐瞒真相并不是保守秘密变得困难的原因，

sentences.en: what have you found is the real psychological cost of keeping secrets?
sentences.zh: 你发现保守秘密真正的心理代价是什么？

sentences.en: So when you're keeping a secret, what you're not doing is you're not letting people in on something
sentences.zh: 当你保守一个秘密时，你没有做的是，你没有让别人参与到某件

sentences.en: that probably really matters to you.
sentences.zh: 可能对你非常重要的事情中来。

sentences.en: Otherwise, if you didn't care about it, you might feel free to talk about it.
sentences.zh: 否则，如果你不在乎它，你可能就会觉得可以自由地谈论它。

sentences.en: But when you choose to be alone with something, you're often worse off for it.
sentences.zh: 但当你选择独自面对某事时，你往往会因此变得更糟。

sentences.en: If it's something you need help with, now you're not getting the help you need.
sentences.zh: 如果这是你需要帮助的事情，现在你得不到所需的帮助。

sentences.en: If it's something you need emotional support for, now you're not getting that either.
sentences.zh: 如果这是你需要情感支持的事情，现在你也得不到支持。

sentences.en: So we're missing out on a lot of things when we're keeping a secret.
sentences.zh: 所以当我们保守秘密时，我们错失了很多东西。

sentences.en: And if you only have a secret to yourself, well, you only have yourself to figure it out.
sentences.zh: 如果你只是把秘密藏在心里，好吧，你就只能靠自己去解决它。

sentences.en: And you're going to find yourself turning that secret over and over in your mind and potentially ruminating on it.
sentences.zh: 你会发现自己不断地在脑海中翻来覆去地想那个秘密，并可能陷入反刍。

sentences.en: And that's where we see the harm.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们看到危害的地方。

sentences.en: It's not having to hide a secret.
sentences.zh: 问题的关键不在于必须隐藏秘密。

sentences.en: It's having to live with it alone.
sentences.zh: 而在于必须独自承受它。

sentences.en: Did you hear any of that in Lauren's story, Michael?
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，你在劳伦的故事里听出这些了吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, and this is what's so interesting about secrecy.
sentences.zh: 是的，这就是秘密最有趣的地方。

sentences.en: I think we think about these sort of specific kinds of secrets, you know, infidelity or cheating or something involving our relationships or finances.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们想到的都是那些特定类型的秘密，你知道，不忠、出轨，或者涉及我们人际关系或财务的事情。

sentences.en: And, you know, something like, say, the timeline of events may not seem like a big deal to certain people, but it's the implications that we're concerned about.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，像事件的时间线这种事情，对某些人来说可能看起来没什么大不了的，但我们关心的是其带来的影响。

sentences.en: And, you know, again, like, you know, I didn't get the sense that people were pushing her to reveal her timeline on those details of her story.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，再说一次，我并没有感觉到有人在逼她透露故事细节中的时间线。

sentences.en: But still, it was something that really mattered to her.
sentences.zh: 但即便如此，那对她来说确实非常重要。

sentences.en: And it clearly was something that was on her mind quite frequently.
sentences.zh: 而且很明显，这件事经常出现在她的脑海里。

sentences.en: One of the things that was striking to me that I thought spoke to the work that you've done is how much what was happening was happening inside her own mind.
sentences.zh: 有一点让我印象深刻，我认为这印证了你的研究工作，那就是她所经历的事情很大程度上发生在她自己的脑海里。

sentences.en: In other words, I'm not even sure this actually is a secret that mattered very much to other people or would have the reputational concerns that she thought it was going to have.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，我甚至不确定这是否真的是一个对其他人很重要，或者会像她所想的那样影响她名声的秘密。

sentences.en: So much of the secret keeping, the effects of secret keeping, the psychological consequences, all of that was happening inside Lauren's head.
sentences.zh: 保守秘密的很大一部分，保守秘密的影响，心理后果，所有这些都发生在劳伦的脑海里。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And that's what we see in our own research, that a lot of it is sort of in your own head and in that way.
sentences.zh: 这正是我们在自己的研究中所看到的，很多东西都在你自己的脑子里，就是这样。

sentences.en: And it's taken psychology a long time to find that idea because we were sort of focused for too long on these sort of moments of hiding.
sentences.zh: 心理学花了很长时间才发现这个观点，因为我们太长时间以来一直专注于那些隐藏的时刻。

sentences.en: That turns out to be not where the real action is in terms of when secrets actually harm us.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，就秘密真正伤害我们而言，那并不是核心所在。

sentences.en: In other words, it's not necessarily the content of a secret that damages our well-being.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，损害我们幸福感的并不一定是秘密的内容。

sentences.en: It's the rumination and worry about what would happen if the secret came to light that ends up being a burden.
sentences.zh: 而是对秘密一旦曝光会发生什么的反复思虑和担忧，这最终成为了一种负担。

sentences.en: Of course, like Lauren, most of us don't foresee all the complexities that can emerge when we keep a secret.
sentences.zh: 当然，像劳伦一样，我们大多数人无法预见保守秘密时可能出现的所有复杂情况。

sentences.en: This is partly why secret keeping is so ubiquitous.
sentences.zh: 这在一定程度上解释了为什么保守秘密如此普遍。

sentences.en: Michael found in one of his studies that we not only tend to keep a lot of secrets, we all tend to keep the same kinds of secrets.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔在他的研究中发现，我们不仅倾向于保守很多秘密，而且我们所有人往往保守的都是同类秘密。

sentences.en: So we asked a couple thousand people about what's a secret you're currently keeping.
sentences.zh: 所以我们问了几千人，你目前保守的秘密是什么？

sentences.en: And we've coded those responses over and over with research assistance and eventually arrived at a set of 38 categories
sentences.zh: 我们和研究助理一遍又一遍地对这些回答进行编码，最终得出了38个类别，

sentences.en: that capture the most common kinds of secrets people keep.
sentences.zh: 涵盖了人们最常保守的秘密类型。

sentences.en: And when I say common, I really mean that these are the common ones that these 38 categories really cover the ground of secrecy pretty well.
sentences.zh: 当我提到“常见”时，我是说这些确实是常见的秘密，这38个类别基本涵盖了秘密的领域。

sentences.en: When we ask someone whether they have any secrets on this list, 97% of people have at least one of the secrets on this liSt.
sentences.zh: 当我们问某人是否有这个清单上的秘密时，97%的人至少有其中一个秘密。

sentences.en: And the average person has 13 of these secrets concurrently.
sentences.zh: 而普通人同时保守着13个这样的秘密。

sentences.en: What kind of secrets are these?
sentences.zh: 这些是什么样的秘密？

sentences.en: So you're not going to be surprised at all.
sentences.zh: 你一点也不会感到惊讶。

sentences.en: It's going to be exactly the kinds of things you think people would be keeping secret.
sentences.zh: 这正是你认为人们会保守的那类秘密。

sentences.en: So things involving relationships, whether that's romantic discontent or infidelity or something we call extra relational thoughts.
sentences.zh: 比如涉及人际关系的事情，无论是对浪漫关系的不满、不忠，还是我们称之为“关系外想法”的事情。

sentences.en: This is a very common secret.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常常见的秘密。

sentences.en: You're in a relationship, you have some kind of romantic thought about another person.
sentences.zh: 你处于一段关系中，却对另一个人产生了某种浪漫的想法。

sentences.en: People tend to not talk about that.
sentences.zh: 人们往往不会谈论这个。

sentences.en: And then things like self-harm, experiences of trauma, discontent at work or discontent with your social life,
sentences.zh: 还有像自残、创伤经历、对工作的不满或对社交生活的不满，

sentences.en: issues around money and habits and addictions and even ambitions.
sentences.zh: 关于金钱、习惯、成瘾甚至野心的问题。

sentences.en: Secret keeping tends to trigger mind games.
sentences.zh: 保守秘密往往会引发心理游戏。

sentences.en: We start out by asking what other people will think of us if they knew our secret.
sentences.zh: 我们一开始会问，如果别人知道我们的秘密，他们会怎么看我们。

sentences.en: We decide they will think less of us, which is why we decide to hide something.
sentences.zh: 我们认定他们会看轻我们，这就是我们决定隐瞒某事的原因。

sentences.en: But soon we find ourselves asking different questions.
sentences.zh: 但很快我们发现自己开始问不同的问题。

sentences.en: What happens if people find out I've hidden something from them?
sentences.zh: 如果人们发现我隐瞒了他们什么，会发生什么？

sentences.en: What will they think of me now?
sentences.zh: 他们现在会怎么看我？

sentences.en: In The Sopranos, the hit TV show about the mob, Tony Soprano does something unthinkable for a macho killer.
sentences.zh: 在讲述黑帮故事的热门电视剧《黑道家族》中，托尼·索普拉诺做了一件对于一个大男子主义杀手来说不可思议的事情。

sentences.en: He suffers a meltdown and goes to see a therapiSt.
sentences.zh: 他精神崩溃了，并去看了一位心理医生。

sentences.en: My understanding from Dr. Cusimano, your family physician, is that you collapsed, possibly a panic attack.
sentences.zh: 据你的家庭医生库西马诺医生说，你晕倒了，可能是恐慌发作。

sentences.en: You were unable to breathe.
sentences.zh: 你当时无法呼吸。

sentences.en: They said it was a panic attack.
sentences.zh: 他们说是恐慌发作。

sentences.en: Of course, all the blood work and the neurological work came back negative.
sentences.zh: 当然，所有的血液检查和神经学检查结果都呈阴性。

sentences.en: And they sent me here.
sentences.zh: 然后他们就把我送到这儿来了。

sentences.en: You don't agree that you had a panic attack?
sentences.zh: 你不认为你当时是恐慌发作？

sentences.en: How are you feeling now?
sentences.zh: 你现在感觉如何？

sentences.en: Good.
sentences.zh: 很好。

sentences.en: Fine.
sentences.zh: 不错。

sentences.en: Back at work.
sentences.zh: 回到工作岗位了。

sentences.en: What line of work are you in?
sentences.zh: 你是从事什么行业的？

sentences.en: Waste management consultant.
sentences.zh: 废物管理顾问。

sentences.en: So this is a scene that you must have thought about as you're doing your research, Michael.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，这一定是你做研究时思考过的场景。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: What I really like about this example is it highlights that a secret can be really burdensome and it's not at all hard to hide.
sentences.zh: 我非常喜欢这个例子，因为它强调了一个秘密可能真的非常沉重，而且隐藏起来一点也不困难。

sentences.en: Tony just said waste management without difficulty and, you know, it's not hard for him to simply just use that as a way to cover the secret.
sentences.zh: 托尼刚才轻描淡写地提到了废物管理，你知道，对他来说，用这个借口来掩盖秘密并不难。

sentences.en: He can just simply say two words and the concealment problem is super easy.
sentences.zh: 他只需要简单说两个词，掩盖问题就迎刃而解了。

sentences.en: And so you would think if the problem with secrecy was having concealment that this would be a really easy secret for him.
sentences.zh: 所以你可能会认为，如果保密的难点在于掩盖，那么对他来说这应该是一个非常容易保守的秘密。

sentences.en: And in fact, it's not.
sentences.zh: 但事实上，并非如此。

sentences.en: It's far from it.
sentences.zh: 远非如此。

sentences.en: But the conceit of the television show is that when the mobster goes to see the psychologist,
sentences.zh: 但这部电视剧的构思是，当黑帮成员去看心理医生时，

sentences.en: at some point this is unthinkable for a mobster to do and it would harm the mobster's reputation.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，这对黑帮成员来说是不可想象的，这会损害他的声誉。

sentences.en: And so Tony then goes to great lengths to try and preserve the secret that he's actually seeing a therapist from his fellow mobsters.
sentences.zh: 因此，托尼不惜一切代价，试图在其他黑帮成员面前保守他正在看心理医生的秘密。

sentences.en: And it starts to affect him at some level in terms of his own perception of himself.
sentences.zh: 这在某种程度上开始影响他对自己认知的看法。

sentences.en: I'm wondering if you can talk about this idea that keeping secrets at some level damages our own view of ourselves and in some ways harms our ability to think of ourselves as being authentic people.
sentences.zh: 我想请教一下，你是否能谈谈这个观点：保守秘密在某种程度上会损害我们对自己的看法，并在某些方面损害我们将自己视为真实个体的能力？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So when we're holding secret back from other people, we're not having these conversations about these things, you know, and this is what we can never realize.
sentences.zh: 所以，当我们对别人隐瞒秘密时，我们就无法就这些事情进行交流，你知道，这就是我们永远无法意识到的。

sentences.en: We don't talk about the secret with other people.
sentences.zh: 我们不与他人谈论这个秘密。

sentences.en: People are generally understanding, especially the people who are close to you.
sentences.zh: 人们通常是善解人意的，尤其是那些与你亲近的人。

sentences.en: You know, maybe it's going to be quite difficult to talk about the secret, but you can.
sentences.zh: 你知道，也许谈论这个秘密会很困难，但你是可以做到的。

sentences.en: And it often makes things better, we find.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，这通常会让事情变得更好。

sentences.en: You've also looked at secret keeping in the context of politics, Michael.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，你还研究过政治背景下的保密行为。

sentences.en: You ran an interesting experiment, I think, right after the 2016 presidential election, which was, of course, between Donald Trump and Hillary Clinton.
sentences.zh: 我想你在2016年总统大选后进行了一项有趣的实验，那次选举当然是在唐纳德·特朗普和希拉里·克林顿之间进行的。

sentences.en: What was the experiment you ran and what did you find?
sentences.zh: 你进行了什么实验？你发现了什么？

sentences.en: So when we ran this study, we were thinking we had a very clear idea about who might be in our study.
sentences.zh: 当我们进行这项研究时，我们认为我们对谁会参与我们的研究有一个非常清晰的想法。

sentences.en: We were asking for people to come online and tell us about their experience.
sentences.zh: 我们邀请人们上网，告诉我们他们的经历。

sentences.en: People who specifically voted for someone but told other people something else, that they voted for someone else or that they voted for no one or whatever it was.
sentences.zh: 那些明确投票给某人，却告诉别人他们投给了其他人，或者投给了谁都没投，或者诸如此类情况的人。

sentences.en: These were people who were not being forthright about their political support and keeping it secret.
sentences.zh: 这些人对自己的政治立场不够坦诚，并将其作为秘密。

sentences.en: We just simply asked people, who are you keeping the secret from?
sentences.zh: 我们只是简单地问人们，你在对谁保守秘密？

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: And, you know, what are the effects?
sentences.zh: 还有，你知道，有什么影响吗？

sentences.en: And these were secrets people were keeping from their friends, family, and even their spouses.
sentences.zh: 这些是人们对朋友、家人甚至配偶隐瞒的秘密。

sentences.en: And we saw far more than we expected, people who were saying that they were secretly supporting Trump.
sentences.zh: 我们看到的比预期的要多得多，人们说他们是在秘密支持特朗普。

sentences.en: And when we asked people why, the number one reason was they were concerned for their reputation.
sentences.zh: 当我们问人们原因时，首要原因是他们担心自己的声誉。

sentences.en: They were concerned that people would think differently of them if they voiced publicly their support for Trump.
sentences.zh: 他们担心如果公开表达对特朗普的支持，人们会以不同的眼光看待他们。

sentences.en: And so it's interesting to think about what that means.
sentences.zh: 所以思考这意味着什么很有趣。

sentences.en: You know, they weren't having conversations with others that maybe they should have had.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们没有与他人进行本该进行的对话。

sentences.en: And sort of the secondary reason people were keeping this a secret was not wanting to get invites and not wanting to create arguments.
sentences.zh: 人们保守这个秘密的次要原因是不想收到邀请，也不想引发争论。

sentences.en: And so if that was the reason why people felt they had to keep their secret, if it was just simply to avoid getting in arguments with the people around them,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果这就是人们觉得必须保守秘密的原因，如果仅仅是为了避免与周围的人发生争论，

sentences.en: that didn't seem to be very harmful.
sentences.zh: 那似乎并没有什么害处。

sentences.en: And so this is this idea, again, coming that when you feel like it may not be easy, but you're doing it for the right thing, we see some less harm in secrecy.
sentences.zh: 所以这又回到了这个观点：当你觉得这可能不容易，但你是在做正确的事情时，我们认为保密带来的伤害较小。

sentences.en: But when participants were especially concerned for their reputation, they found themselves having to think about the secret quite a bit.
sentences.zh: 但当参与者特别担心自己的声誉时，他们发现自己不得不经常思考这个秘密。

sentences.en: And the more they did so, the less authentic they felt with the people around them.
sentences.zh: 他们思考得越多，在周围人面前就越感到不真实。

sentences.en: Examining the intention behind a secret can be a good way to understand what and whether it will cost you to keep it hidden.
sentences.zh: 审视秘密背后的意图，是了解保守秘密是否会让你付出代价的好方法。

sentences.en: It's easy, for example, to shrug off a secret designed to avoid a political tiff with a co-worker.
sentences.zh: 例如，为了避免与同事发生政治争执而保守秘密是很容易的。

sentences.en: Both you and your colleague now, there are things you keep from each other to make work life go smoothly.
sentences.zh: 你和你的同事现在都知道，为了让工作生活顺利进行，你们之间有些事情是互相隐瞒的。

sentences.en: But other secrets are not so easy to brush away.
sentences.zh: 但其他秘密就没那么容易被忽略了。

sentences.en: That's because these secrets reveal what you think of others, what you think they think of you.
sentences.zh: 这是因为这些秘密揭示了你对他人的看法，以及你认为他们对你的看法。

sentences.en: They reveal your insecurities, your vulnerabilities.
sentences.zh: 它们揭示了你的不安全感和脆弱性。

sentences.en: These secrets tend to produce one of the most damaging consequences to secret keeping.
sentences.zh: 这些秘密往往会产生保守秘密最有害的后果之一。

sentences.en: It's something that Michael calls mind-wandering.
sentences.zh: 这就是迈克尔所说的“思绪游离”。

sentences.en: Because a secret often deals with something that's important to you or ongoing,
sentences.zh: 因为秘密通常涉及对你重要或正在进行的事情，

sentences.en: because a secret often feels unresolved, because you haven't had the conversations you would normally have,
sentences.zh: 因为秘密通常感觉没有解决，因为你没有进行本该进行的对话，

sentences.en: our minds return to unresolved concerns and outstanding intentions and ongoing issues frequently,
sentences.zh: 我们的思绪会频繁回到未解决的担忧、未完成的意图和正在进行的问题上，

sentences.en: because those are the things that require our attention.
sentences.zh: 因为这些是需要我们关注的事情。

sentences.en: If something needs some kind of resolution or you need to work on something,
sentences.zh: 如果某事需要某种解决，或者你需要处理某事，

sentences.en: whether you like it or not, your mind is going to turn to it over and over.
sentences.zh: 无论你是否愿意，你的思绪都会反复回到它上面。

sentences.en: And people don't often put on their calendar,
sentences.zh: 人们通常不会在日历上标注，

sentences.en: okay, from 10 a.m.
sentences.zh: 好吧，从上午10点

sentences.en: to 10.30, I'm going to think about my secret.
sentences.zh: 到10点半，我要思考我的秘密。

sentences.en: People don't plan to think about their secret, but their secret comes to mind anyway.
sentences.zh: 人们不会计划去思考他们的秘密，但秘密还是会不由自主地浮现在脑海中。

sentences.en: And so that's why we describe it as mind-wandering.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是我们将其描述为“思绪游离”的原因。

sentences.en: There's certain features about a secret that make it that your attention,
sentences.zh: 秘密有一些特定的特征，使得你的注意力，

sentences.en: when you're not focused on a work task, when you're not focused on the thing in front of you,
sentences.zh: 当你没有专注于工作任务，当你没有专注于眼前的事情时，

sentences.en: your mind can be drawn toward your secret.
sentences.zh: 你的思绪会被吸引到你的秘密上。

sentences.en: Things make you think of it.
sentences.zh: 事物让你想起它。

sentences.en: Things remind you of it.
sentences.zh: 事物提醒你它。

sentences.en: And especially when it's something that you feel not good about or you feel alone with
sentences.zh: 尤其是当你对它感觉不好，或者感到孤独，

sentences.en: or you feel inauthentic for, once that secret comes to mind, it can be hard to put it down.
sentences.zh: 或者因为保守它而感到不真实时，一旦秘密浮现，就很难放下。

sentences.en: And you talk at one point in your research studies about the difference between experiencing shame
sentences.zh: 你在研究中曾谈到过在保守秘密时，体验羞耻感

sentences.en: and experiencing guilt when it comes to secrets.
sentences.zh: 与体验内疚感之间的区别。

sentences.en: I'm wondering if you can talk about that distinction,
sentences.zh: 我想请教你谈谈这种区别，

sentences.en: but also talk about it in the context of this mind-wandering idea.
sentences.zh: 同时也请在“思绪游离”这个概念的背景下谈谈它。

sentences.en: Are secrets that are more tied to shame more likely to cause our minds to return to them over and over again?
sentences.zh: 与羞耻感联系更紧密的秘密，是否更容易导致我们的思绪反复回到它们身上？

sentences.en: Or is guilt more likely to produce mind-wandering?
sentences.zh: 还是内疚感更容易产生思绪游离？

sentences.en: Yeah, so psychologists make this very important distinction between these two words.
sentences.zh: 是的，心理学家在这两个词之间做出了非常重要的区分。

sentences.en: And the idea is that when you feel guilty, you feel that something you've done is wrong.
sentences.zh: 其观点是，当你感到内疚时，你会觉得你所做的事情是错误的。

sentences.en: You've caused some harm.
sentences.zh: 你造成了一些伤害。

sentences.en: Your actions were wrong.
sentences.zh: 你的行为是错误的。

sentences.en: So when people feel guilty, they're more likely to feel remorse and be interested in making amends.
sentences.zh: 所以当人们感到内疚时，他们更有可能感到懊悔，并有兴趣进行弥补。

sentences.en: But when you feel ashamed, you don't think about how your behavior was wrong.
sentences.zh: 但当你感到羞耻时，你不会去想你的行为哪里错了。

sentences.en: You think about how there's something wrong with you.
sentences.zh: 你会去想你这个人本身有什么问题。

sentences.en: When people feel ashamed, they feel like they're a bad person.
sentences.zh: 当人们感到羞耻时，他们觉得自己是个坏人。

sentences.en: And they feel helpless and frozen.
sentences.zh: 他们感到无助和僵化。

sentences.en: And there's nothing they can do about it.
sentences.zh: 而且他们对此无能为力。

sentences.en: And so we find that when secrets make people feel ashamed,
sentences.zh: 所以我们发现，当秘密让人们感到羞耻时，

sentences.en: they're much more likely to have their mind turn over the secret over and over.
sentences.zh: 他们更有可能反复思索这个秘密。

sentences.en: And the secret comes to mind much more frequently.
sentences.zh: 而且秘密浮现在脑海中的频率要高得多。

sentences.en: So when most of us think of secrets, I think the metaphor that I think jumps to mind is this metaphor of a shield.
sentences.zh: 所以当我们大多数人想到秘密时，我想脑海中浮现的隐喻是“盾牌”的隐喻。

sentences.en: We have this vision of someone trying to pry the secret out of us
sentences.zh: 我们脑海中有一个画面：有人试图从我们这里探听秘密，

sentences.en: and us trying to sort of hold the shield up to sort of defend ourselves
sentences.zh: 而我们试图举起盾牌来保护自己，

sentences.en: or defend ourselves against someone breaking through our defenses.
sentences.zh: 或者保护自己免受他人突破我们的防线。

sentences.en: But I think the picture that you're painting here is almost a different kind of metaphor,
sentences.zh: 但我认为你在这里描绘的画面几乎是一种不同的隐喻，

sentences.en: that it's really not the shield that really is motivating how we're thinking about secrets that are in our minds.
sentences.zh: 真正驱动我们思考心中秘密的，其实并不是盾牌。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You know, at the end of the day, people want to talk about these things.
sentences.zh: 你知道，归根结底，人们是想谈论这些事情的。

sentences.en: And secrecy is us stopping ourselves from doing so.
sentences.zh: 而保密是我们阻止自己这样做。

sentences.en: And so you're right.
sentences.zh: 所以你是对的。

sentences.en: It's not a shield.
sentences.zh: 它不是盾牌。

sentences.en: It's like a cork is the better metaphor, perhaps.
sentences.zh: 也许“瓶塞”是更好的隐喻。

sentences.en: We normally talk to other people to get their help.
sentences.zh: 我们通常会与他人交谈以获得他们的帮助。

sentences.en: And this is an instance where we're plugging that.
sentences.zh: 而这是一种我们正在堵住这种情况的实例。

sentences.en: We're not allowing that to happen.
sentences.zh: 我们不允许这种情况发生。

sentences.en: And that has all these harmful consequences.
sentences.zh: 这会带来所有这些有害的后果。

sentences.en: When we come back, the effects of secrets on feelings of isolation
sentences.zh: 回来后，我们将探讨秘密对孤独感的影响，

sentences.en: and the paradoxical effect of being the owner of secrets in the workplace.
sentences.zh: 以及在职场中作为秘密持有者的矛盾效应。

sentences.en: You're listening to Hidden Brain, and I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 你正在收听的是《隐藏的大脑》，我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: Psychologist Michael Slepian studies the effects of keeping secrets and being the holder of secrets.
sentences.zh: 心理学家迈克尔·斯莱皮安研究保守秘密和作为秘密持有者的影响。

sentences.en: He finds that secrets can have pervasive effects in our lives.
sentences.zh: 他发现秘密会对我们的生活产生普遍的影响。

sentences.en: They make us feel less authentic, especially if our minds are constantly wandering back to the secret
sentences.zh: 它们让我们感到不那么真实，尤其是如果我们的思绪不断游离回到秘密上，

sentences.en: and wondering when we are going to reveal all.
sentences.zh: 并想知道我们何时会全盘托出。

sentences.en: Michael, you started your exploration of secrets in part because you were interested in the metaphors people use
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，你开始探索秘密的部分原因是由于你对人们谈论秘密时使用的隐喻感兴趣，

sentences.en: when they talk about secrets, you know, when they talk about the burden of a secret, for example.
sentences.zh: 你知道，比如当他们谈论秘密的负担时。

sentences.en: Talk to me about this idea that in some ways you started out looking at the role that metaphors might play
sentences.zh: 跟我谈谈这个观点：在某种程度上，你最初是研究隐喻可能扮演的角色，

sentences.en: and then you discovered something actually quite surprising when you conducted experiments into this.
sentences.zh: 然后当你进行相关实验时，你发现了一些非常令人惊讶的事情。

sentences.en: Yeah, so people have this curious way of talking about secrets.
sentences.zh: 是的，人们谈论秘密的方式很奇特。

sentences.en: People will say that they have a heavy secret or a secret weighs them down
sentences.zh: 人们会说他们有一个沉重的秘密，或者秘密让他们感到压抑，

sentences.en: or they have to carry a secret around with them.
sentences.zh: 或者他们必须随身携带一个秘密。

sentences.en: People talk about a secret almost as if it's this physical weight that they are weighed down by
sentences.zh: 人们谈论秘密时，几乎就像它是一种让他们感到压抑的物理重量，

sentences.en: and have to carry with them.
sentences.zh: 并且必须随身携带。

sentences.en: So our original studies were just interested in learning about that metaphor.
sentences.zh: 所以我们最初的研究只是想了解那个隐喻。

sentences.en: Is that just something, is that just a figure of speech?
sentences.zh: 那仅仅是某种东西吗，那仅仅是一个修辞手法吗？

sentences.en: Or does that metaphor reflect actually how we think about secrets in a more deep way?
sentences.zh: 还是那个隐喻实际上反映了我们更深层次思考秘密的方式？

sentences.en: In a series of studies, Michael asked people to think about secrets
sentences.zh: 在一系列研究中，迈克尔请人们思考秘密，

sentences.en: and then asked them to judge the steepness of hills or other physical tasks.
sentences.zh: 然后请他们判断山坡的陡峭程度或其他身体任务。

sentences.en: Volunteers judged hills as steeper and distances as further when they were burdened with a secret.
sentences.zh: 当志愿者背负着秘密时，他们判断山坡更陡，距离更远。

sentences.en: It's as if the secret had spilled into the physical world and was weighing them down.
sentences.zh: 就好像秘密已经溢出到物理世界中，并压得他们喘不过气来。

sentences.en: You can see this in one scene in the TV show The Office.
sentences.zh: 你可以在电视剧《办公室》的一个场景中看到这一点。

sentences.en: The character Kevin successfully manages to hold on to the secret
sentences.zh: 角色凯文成功地保守住了秘密，

sentences.en: that one of his colleagues is having an affair with another colleague's spouse.
sentences.zh: 即他的一位同事正与另一位同事的配偶有染。

sentences.en: What's striking to me, Michael, is the relief that we hear in Kevin's voice
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，让我印象深刻的是，当凯文不再需要保守秘密时，

sentences.en: when he no longer has to hold on to the secret.
sentences.zh: 我们从他的声音中听到的那种解脱感。

sentences.en: That speaks exactly to what you're just talking about.
sentences.zh: 这正是你刚才所谈论的内容。

sentences.en: Yeah, it feels good to get it off our chest, but just getting it off your chest isn't enough.
sentences.zh: 是的，说出来感觉很好，但仅仅说出来是不够的。

sentences.en: It's having a conversation about that secret, which is actually when you get the help that you need.
sentences.zh: 与人谈论那个秘密，才是你真正获得所需帮助的时候。

sentences.en: And so, for example, revealing a secret anonymously online,
sentences.zh: 所以，例如，在网上匿名揭露一个秘密，

sentences.en: that does feel really good to sort of anonymously just put your secret out in the world,
sentences.zh: 匿名地把你的秘密公之于众确实感觉很好，

sentences.en: but it's not as good as talking to another person about it.
sentences.zh: 但这不如与另一个人谈论它来得好。

sentences.en: In 2019, Michael took part in a project led by the New York City-based organization Subway Therapy
sentences.zh: 2019年，迈克尔参与了一个由纽约市组织“地铁疗法”领导的项目，

sentences.en: to explore this very idea.
sentences.zh: 旨在探索这个想法。

sentences.en: The study involved setting up a telephone booth in Central Park.
sentences.zh: 这项研究包括在中央公园设置一个电话亭。

sentences.en: But it wasn't just any telephone booth.
sentences.zh: 但它不仅仅是任何电话亭。

sentences.en: It said secret telephone, get something off your chest,
sentences.zh: 上面写着“秘密电话，说出你的心事”，

sentences.en: and if you picked up the receiver, you could listen to secrets
sentences.zh: 如果你拿起听筒，你可以听到人们之前分享给这个电话的秘密，

sentences.en: people had previously shared with the phone, and you could leave your own.
sentences.zh: 你也可以留下你自己的秘密。

sentences.en: I gave up my keto diet because of waffles.
sentences.zh: 我因为华夫饼放弃了生酮饮食。

sentences.en: Dating is exhausting, and I'm afraid I'm going to die alone.
sentences.zh: 约会太累了，我怕我会孤独终老。

sentences.en: I like to eat egg salad on the toilet.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢在马桶上吃鸡蛋沙拉。

sentences.en: Where do I?
sentences.zh: 我该去哪儿？

sentences.en: So this speaks to what you just said a second ago.
sentences.zh: 所以这印证了你刚才说的话。

sentences.en: So in some ways, this was a way for people to get the secrets off their chest,
sentences.zh: 所以从某种程度上说，这是人们说出心事的一种方式，

sentences.en: but not necessarily to have a conversation with someone about it.
sentences.zh: 但不一定能就此与人进行对话。

sentences.en: Yeah, and you know, if your starting point is you haven't told a single soul,
sentences.zh: 是的，你知道，如果你的出发点是你还没有告诉任何人，

sentences.en: and you think you'll never will,
sentences.zh: 而你认为你永远不会说出来，

sentences.en: getting it off your chest is a really great starting point,
sentences.zh: 把心事倾诉出来是一个非常好的起点，

sentences.en: because you realize this is something I can say out loud.
sentences.zh: 因为你会意识到，原来这是我可以大声说出来的事情。

sentences.en: Maybe this is something I can move forward on.
sentences.zh: 也许这是我可以继续前进的事情。

sentences.en: Maybe this is not so bad.
sentences.zh: 也许这并没有那么糟糕。

sentences.en: Maybe it's not as bad as I think.
